correctness.rationale: The endpoint reachability Gramian for a single coordinate activation at backward time s is diagonal with w_i=integral_{sigma=i} exp(-2lambda_i s)ds; worst Euclidean target energy is 1/min_i w_i when each positive, infinite otherwise. Monotone primitive F_lambda ensures unique ordered cuts having identical integrals m. The dual p_i>0 chosen at adjacent switch crossings makes g_i(s)=p_i exp(-2lambda_i s) the unique upper envelope on its intended interval (all nonneighbor crossings are convex combinations of intervening cuts). For every other measurable schedule, min_i w_i<=sum p_i w_i<=integral max_i g_i=sum p_i m=m. Equality in the strict envelope except finite crossings forces the same schedule almost everywhere. Independent double-precision bisection for n=2,(lambda1,lambda2,T)=(2,1,1) gave cut 0.3397459832093852,m=0.18576957648171977,1/m=5.383012756657723 and correctly ordered dual envelope on 1000 points. Numerical tests only support the exact global proof.
residual_risks: The construction presupposes distinct positive rates, no switching cost, no minimum dwell and equal unit actuator gains.

value.rationale: The exact unique time allocation among an uncountable class of measurable one-actuator schedules solves a natural worst-case controllability-energy design problem. The scalar bisection and strict one-pass ordered switching rule replace generic high-dimensional combinatorial scheduling and offer an analytically sharp benchmark for diagonal control.
residual_risks: Not applicable directly to coupled dynamics, switching penalties, multiple channels or discrete time.

final_claim: For every n>=2, T>0 and strictly ordered positive diagonal rates lambda_1>...>lambda_n, among all measurable preselected one-coordinate-at-a-time actuator schedules, the unique minimizer up to null sets of worst-case terminal minimum energy is the backward-time sorted contiguous schedule with equal diagonal Gramian entries m, determined by one monotone scalar root; worst-case energy equals 1/m.
limitations: Rates strictly decreasing and positive; equal rates lose strict uniqueness and are excluded.
Any measurable schedule may switch rapidly; no implementation delay or switching cost.
